title: Visible window for a fixed-height list
summary: Compute which rows a virtualised list should render from offsets, like getItemLayout.
prompt: Rows all have the same height. Write `itemLayout(index, height)` returning `{ length, offset, index }`, and `visibleRange({ offset, viewport, itemHeight, count, overscan })` returning `{ first, last }`: the inclusive indices of rows that intersect `[offset, offset + viewport)`, widened by `overscan` rows on each side and clamped to `0..count - 1`. If `count` is `0`, return `{ first: 0, last: -1 }`. A row that only touches the bottom edge is not visible. There is no React Native runtime here, so this is modelled as plain TypeScript.
hints: The first visible row is `Math.floor(offset / itemHeight)`.
The last visible row is `Math.ceil((offset + viewport) / itemHeight) - 1`.
